title: RAW: previous-word length selects a reversible cyclic cut inside the next word
summary: A marker-free, noncompressing contextual writer cyclically rotates each source word by the preceding word length modulo its own length, then applies one fixed symbol bijection. The reader observes both needed lengths and reverses the cut. Source text distinctions are preserved without editing, references or a wordbook. No native fit or historical attestation claimed.

complete_rule.source_domain: Any finite sequence of records, each a finite list of nonempty words over exactly22abstract source units. Teaching examples use a..v; those are arbitrary labels, not a chosen language. Unsupported sourceunits are outside the declared domain, never normalized or assigned native meanings.
complete_rule.codebook: One fixed bijection sigma between these22sourceunits and22writtenunits. No initial control sign, escape, hidden header, deletion, insertion or special endpoint form.
complete_rule.state: One integer m, the length of the previous source word. Set m=0 at an explicitly supplied record boundary. Actual Voynich lines/paragraphs are not identified with resets by this proposal.
complete_rule.encoder: For nonempty current word w of lengthn, set s=m mod n. Emit sigma(w[s:]+w[:s]) as one written group, preserve the word separator, then set m=n. At s=0 emit the unrotated word. The word is copied once, starting at the s+1st source position and wrapping once.
complete_rule.reader: Know m from the preceding OUTPUTgroup length, or0at the same supplied record start. Apply sigma inverse to current output y oflengthn, set s=m mod n, and rightrotate bys: w=y[n-s:]+y[:n-s] when s>0, otherwisew=y. Set m=n. Thus the reader never needs an unobserved lexical identity to choose the cut.
complete_rule.inverse_proof: Length is unchanged, so encoder andreader maintain identicalm. Leftrotation bys andrightrotation bys are inversepermutations; sigma is bijective. Inductionoverwords recovers exactsource sequence andboundaries.
